correctness.rationale: For I≠S, 0 is excluded from S−I, which contains the entire conductor tail and only possible additional shifts z in [m,2m−h−1]. Intersecting S−z over those shifts excludes in the low band precisely the union of their full length-h windows [2m−h−z,2m−1−z]. Any subset of shifts together with the conductor tail gives a reflexive intersection by the antitone colon Galois relation; the tail forbids negatives and all such intersections contain the high band. The union characterization is equivalent to every omitted run having length at least h, including the empty complement. S is fixed separately. Once the high gaps have been included, the ideal contains every integer ≥m, so addition by positive S-elements cannot leave it. This is the reason ideal closure holds; the frozen sentence saying such sums are either in H or ≥2m misses sums in the middle band. The j zero-run lengths give weak compositions of r−jh, and the separating ones give binom(n−r+1,j); out-of-range counts are understood as zero. Alternating one- and zero-runs have series A=z/(1−z) and B=(uz)^h/(1−uz), and their word series is (1+A)(1+B)/(1−AB), yielding the asserted generating functions, extreme cases, and the extra contribution of S. An independently written translate-intersection and word-automaton check (python3 /workspace/reproductions/reflexive_ideals.py) reproduced the complete ideal sets in 45 parameter pairs through m=10 and all genus coefficients in 260 (n,h) pairs. These are finite checks supplementing the proof.
